title: "Field guide"
subtitle: "The lab's pipelines, read like a map"
description: "Annotated tours of MicroCPipe, TTpipe and ChromSimPipe, with a table of where each idea from the course shows up in real code."
---

The modules teach Snakemake on RegPipe, a pipeline built for the course. The field guide shows
the same ideas in the three pipelines the lab actually runs:

- [MicroCPipe](microcpipe.qmd): Micro-C, FASTQ to contact maps (`.cool`, `.mcool`, `.hic`) and a
  QC dashboard. The smallest of the three and the closest to RegPipe. Start here.
- [TTpipe](ttpipe.qmd): TT-seq, FASTQ to stranded tracks, gene counts, DESeq2 and GSEA. The largest,
  with switches that turn whole halves of the workflow on and off.
- [ChromSimPipe](chromsimpipe.qmd): loop-extrusion polymer simulations on GPUs, compared with
  Hi-C. Outputs are folders, not files, and the job count multiplies four ways.
- [How our pipelines compare to community conventions](conventions.qmd): the Snakemake workflow
  catalog's layout next to ours, what `snakemake --lint` says, and what is worth changing.

Each pipeline page has the same parts: what the pipeline does biologically, its rule graph, a
walk from inputs to outputs, "Concepts in the wild" sections with the real code and a line-by-line
reading, a short list of what you would change, and a few open exercises with answers.

All code is pulled from the repositories at a fixed commit, and each block links to the same lines
on GitHub, so what you read here is what ran. You can read a page after the matching module, or
all of them after module 8. Nothing in the modules depends on the field guide.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use this with the modules

Finished a module? Find its rows in the table below and follow one link per pipeline. Seeing the
same idea written three ways, by the same person at different times, is the fastest way to tell
what is a rule of Snakemake and what is one person's habit.
:::

## Three pipelines, one pattern {#pattern}

All three share a layout, which RegPipe copies:

```
<Name>.sh  unlock.sh  <Name>Samplesheet.txt
config/<Name>Config.yaml  config/requirements.txt
profiles/<site>/{config.yaml, env.sh}
workflows/<Name>.snakefile  workflows/rules/*.smk
envs/*.yml  scripts/  tests/  docs/
```

The pattern comes from the PhanstielLab pipelines (dietJuicer, bagPipes): edit a samplesheet and a
config, pick a site profile once, then submit one launcher. Where the three differ, the field guide
says which version to copy. Usually it is MicroCPipe's, because its launcher and profiles carry the most fixes.
